title: Align client-encoded lengths with server token crediting for attachments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Investigate and fix inconsistencies between client-side reported lengths/byte counts for multipart attachments (base64, gzip, chunked) and server-side token crediting. We’ve observed customers receiving discrepant token charges when attachments are sent via different encodings or when clients perform on-the-fly normalization (newline conversions, unicode normalization, NFKC/NFKD, or pre-tokenization). This ticket scopes a deterministic normalization and attribution flow so that identical logical inputs always produce identical billed token counts, regardless of encoding/transport quirks.
acceptance_criteria: Define canonical normalization rules used by server before tokenization and publish them to SDK docs (line endings, unicode normalization, whitespace collapse for attachments).

Server-meters must produce identical token counts for: raw utf-8, base64-wrapped payloads, gzip-compressed-then-base64 payloads (after canonical normalization), and chunked multipart uploads when reassembled.
Add cross-checking telemetry metric: client_length_vs_server_token_delta with thresholds and alerting when delta > 2% for any customer over a 1-hour window.
Create an e2e test harness that runs 500 randomized transforms (encodings, normalizations) and asserts stable billed tokens across transformations.
Rollout plan with canary for 5% of host accounts and automatic rollback if customer_impact metric spikes > 5x baseline.
technical_notes: Root cause hypothesis: clients apply different normalization steps and some SDKs (older Python/JS) send bytes that the server treats as distinct tokenization input leading to off-by-one token splits. In other cases, base64 vs raw paths bypass server prefix-stripping optimizations and cause different tokenizer paths to be used.

Proposed server change: canonicalize attachments into a normalized byte sequence before any tokenization-based metering. Normalization components: detect and decode known wrappers (base64, multipart boundary reassembly), optional decompression if flagged by Content-Encoding, apply Unicode NFKC, normalize CRLF to LF, and strip leading/trailing zero-width spaces unless flagged as significant.

API/SDK side: emit an optional header X-Client-Canonical-Length and X-Client-Canonical-Hash when SDKs perform the same normalization; server will compare hashes and emit a disagreement metric to help customers upgrade SDKs.

We must preserve binary attachments semantics for non-text attachments — only apply text normalization when Content-Type indicates text/* or application/json. For unknown content-types, only decode wrappers and do not apply unicode normalization.
Performance: canonicalization must be fast and stream-friendly. Implement streaming normalization that operates on buffer windows and avoids full in-memory expansion for large attachments (> 50MB).
Metering implication: tokenization step will now always run on canonicalized stream; update billing docs and notify customers of token count determinism improvement.

comments: 2025-01-28 Asha Patel: Initial investigation — surfaced by enterprise customer B via support ticket. Example repros attached. Hypothesis: discrepancy introduced by mixed base64 and raw upload paths.

2025-02-03 Miguel Alvarez: Implemented prototype normalizer in local branch. Streaming path validated on small samples. Performance microbenchmarks show 5% CPU overhead on p10 attachments; need to optimize buffer sizing.

2025-02-17 Asha Patel: Reviewed prototype. Key concern: unicode normalization might change byte-level semantics for some clients. Decided to only apply NFKC on text/* and application/json content types. Added requirement to not modify binary payloads.
2025-02-22 SRE (Liu Chen): Added temporary high-cardinality debug flag to collect client vs server hashes for 1% of requests — low overhead confirmed in staging.

2025-03-01 Miguel Alvarez: Started integration tests. Found edge-case where chunked reassembly boundary cut a UTF-8 multi-byte sequence; fixed by introducing boundary-aware reassembly that ensures valid UTF-8 frames before normalization.
2025-03-04 Asha Patel: Drafted customer communication and SDK spec for X-Client-Canonical-* headers. Planning 2-week canary after QA signoff.
